## Positivity-limiter meters: `limcut`, `thetamin`, `thetasevere` (`_positivity_severe`) {#sec-ch13-limiter-meters}

### Summary

The limiter scales each species flux leaving a cell by a factor $\Theta \in [0,1]$, so that the cell cannot be
drained below zero in a stage. The meters turn those factors into three numbers a reader can watch. `thetamin=`
is the smallest $\Theta$ so far. `thetasevere=` counts the (cell, species) entries cut hard enough to matter.
`limcut=` is the fraction of the offered $x_1$ flux that was cut.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Counts, over the run, how hard the species flux-positivity limiter of @sec-ch08 acted, @eq-ch13-limiter-severe.

**Data.** Reads the limiter factors $\Theta$ and the offered $x_1$ fluxes of each stage; prints `thetamin=`, `thetasevere=`, `limcut=`.

**Placement.** A census in `HydroImpl::forward` each stage; printed in the run-to-date group of the cycle line.

**Activation.** With species: `limiter: true`, or a face-flux covariance row in $x_2$ or $x_3$ (on by default).

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact counts; `limcut` sees the $x_1$ flux only.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch13-limiter-meters-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho_{y,i}$ [kg m$^{-3}$] the density of one species in cell $i$;
$D_i$ [kg] the mass its faces would remove in the stage; $\mathcal M_i$ [kg] the cell's gas mass, dry plus all
species; $n_{\mathrm{ulp}}$ the round-off multiple. $\Theta$ (the limiter's donor factor), $V_i$, $\Delta t$[^rg-da0c83a08e15] and
$\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

The census runs whenever the run carries species and either `equation-of-state/limiter` is true or the stage added a
face-flux covariance row in $x_2$ or $x_3$: the gate is `(limiter() || cov2 || cov3) && ny > 0`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The covariance rows exist with `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE`
on, its default, on a resolved $x_2$ or $x_3$ axis, unless $n_1<3$ or the equation of state is shallow water. So in a
two- or three-dimensional moist run the limiter acts and the meters count at the defaults, with `limiter: false`.

### Derivation

For a species of density $\rho_y$ in cell $i$, with $D_i$ the mass its faces would remove in the stage step
$\Delta t$, the limiter factor is
$\Theta_i = \min\big(1, (1-4096\epsilon_{\mathrm m})\,\rho_{y,i}V_i/D_i\big)$ where $D_i > 0$, and 1 elsewhere. Where the
dry air of the cell is itself over-drained in the stage, the stage relaxes that factor toward the dry air's before the
census (@eq-ch08-theta-relax), so the census reads the relaxed factor: below, $\Theta_i$ is the factor after the
relaxation, a hit is an entry whose relaxed factor is below 1, and $D_i$ is still the unrelaxed drain of the species.
The mass held back is $(1-\Theta_i)D_i$. An entry is severe when

$$
\Theta_i < 0.9 \quad\text{and}\quad (1-\Theta_i)\,D_i > n_{\mathrm{ulp}}\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,\mathcal M_i ,
$$ {#eq-ch13-limiter-severe}

with $\mathcal M_i$ the cell's gas mass, dry plus all species, and $n_{\mathrm{ulp}} = 4096$ in float64 or 64 in float32.
The second condition keeps round-off events out of the count. The thresholds are $9.09\times10^{-13}$ and
$7.63\times10^{-6}$ of the gas mass [check `src/snapy_report/ch13/checks/limiter_meters_check.py`, output
`limiter_meters_check.out`, `[C3]`].

On a settling column where $\Delta t\,|v_{\mathrm{sed}}|/\Delta x = 2$ in five draining cells, $\Theta$ is
$1/2$ in those cells. That gives five hits, five severe entries, `thetamin` $1/2$ and `limcut` $1/2$, each to
$5\times10^{-13}$, the size of the $4096\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ margin (`[C1]`). An empty cell drained by a $10^{-20}$ face flux
has $\Theta = 0$ and counts as a hit, but not as severe (`[C2]`). When the limiter never cuts, `thetamin` stays at
its initial 1, `thetasevere` at 0, and `limcut` is not printed (`[C4]`).

Why a round-off drain is not counted as severe, in three steps:

1. *An empty cell has $\Theta=0$ at any $\Delta t$.* A cell with $\rho_y=0$ drained by any positive face flux gets
   $\Theta=0$, so $\Theta<0.9$ alone would count it.
2. *Its withheld mass is the drain.* $(1-\Theta)D_i=D_i$, the face flux times $\Delta t$, which for a round-off
   flux is of order $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ of the neighbour's gas mass.
3. *The second test compares it with round-off.* `withheld > positivity_roundoff(dtype) * cell_mass` requires more
   than $n_{\mathrm{ulp}}\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\mathcal M_i$, so a $10^{-20}$ drain is a hit, not severe (`[C2]`).

In the code, @eq-ch13-limiter-severe is the census into `_positivity_severe`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch13-limiter-meters for the settling column of the check. The check ports the plain factor: its column has
no dry mass flux, so the dry-air factor is 1 there and the relaxation of @eq-ch08-theta-relax leaves $\Theta$
unchanged; a settling cell would keep its plain factor in any case (@sec-ch08-carry).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-limiter-meters
#| fig-cap: "The settling column of the check. Left: the limiter factor $\\Theta$ of each cell; the five draining cells have $\\Theta=1/2$, below the severe threshold 0.9 (vermillion). Right: the offered $|F|$ of each face (orange) and the part the limiter cut (vermillion); limcut is the sum of the cuts over the sum of the offers, here 1/2."
#| fig-alt: "Two bar charts: Theta per cell, one bar at 1 and five at 0.5 under a dashed line at 0.9; and paired offered and cut flux bars on five faces, the cut bars half the offered ones."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch13.figures.fig_limiter_meters import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The factor comes from `flux_positivity_theta`, with the margin `margin` of 4096 ulp in every precision
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}). The round-off bound of the severe test is `positivity_roundoff`, from the
two constants `kPositivityRoundoffUlp` and `kPositivityRoundoffUlpFloat` ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp kPositivityRoundoffUlpFloat >}}, {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp kPositivityRoundoffUlp >}}).
In each stage, `HydroImpl::forward` takes a census of the interior entries before the ghost fill. It adds the
entries with $\Theta<1$ to `_positivity_hits`, the severe ones to `_positivity_severe`, and lowers
`_positivity_min` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). After the fluxes are scaled, it adds the offered
interior $x_1$ flux magnitude to `_lim_flux` and the cut to `_lim_cut` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

The five meters are module buffers set up with `register_buffer` at construction: 0 for the counts and sums, 1
for the minimum ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). The same `reset` registers a sixth counter
beside them, `conversion_trips`, but only when `dynamics/conversion-order` is 4: it is not a limiter meter and
is described with the scheme that fills it (@sec-ch04-conv4). At the default key the buffer does not exist, so
a reader listing the module's buffers sees five. The cycle line sums the counts and the two flux totals over
blocks and ranks, takes the MIN of $\Theta$, and prints the ratio only when the offered total is positive, through
`limcut` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}). The hit count is not printed. It is read by the step acceptance
(@sec-ch07-redo) through the EOS[^rg-b14888cbe998] limiter marks, `limiter_hits` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::limiter_hits >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** The meters count whenever the limiter acts; to act in one dimension too, turn it on:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamics`[^rg-113abfd374b7], `equation-of-state`[^rg-92353019d76a], `limiter`[^rg-17f1cd4e9131].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state:
    type: ideal-moist
    limiter: true
```

`ideal-moist` needs the species and reactions of a moist deck, so add these keys to a copy of `bryan.yaml`, not to a
dry deck such as `straka_single.yaml`, where construction stops with "[IdealMoist] thermo pointer is null".

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing: the meters have no option, and `thetamin=` and `thetasevere=` are printed on
every cycle line ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}); `limcut=` only when the offered
$x_1$ flux is positive.

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch13-limiter-severe** ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
_positivity_hits += (ti < 1.).sum();                                   // Theta < 1
auto withheld = ((1. - theta) * drain).index(cells).to(torch::kFloat64);  // (1 - Theta) D
auto above = withheld > positivity_roundoff(u.scalar_type()) * cell_mass...;  // > n_ulp eps_m M_i
_positivity_severe += ((ti < 0.9) & above).sum();
torch::minimum_out(_positivity_min, _positivity_min, ti.min());        // thetamin
```

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| limiter factor | {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}} | `flux_positivity_theta` | |
| round-off constants | {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp kPositivityRoundoffUlpFloat >}}, {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp kPositivityRoundoffUlp >}} | `kPositivityRoundoffUlp` | |
| census | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `_positivity_severe` | `equation-of-state/limiter`, or face-flux covariance rows added |
| cut and offered flux | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `_lim_cut` | |
| buffers | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `register_buffer` | |
| the sixth counter, not a limiter meter | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `conversion_trips` | `dynamics/conversion-order` 4 |
| accessors | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl >}} | `positivity_min` | |
| printing | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}} | `thetasevere` | |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`limcut` measures the $x_1$ flux only. A run whose limiter acts in $x_2$ or $x_3$ shows it in `thetamin` and
`thetasevere`, not in `limcut`.
:::

1. **Initial values.** A run whose limiter never cut prints `thetamin=1` and `thetasevere=0`. That reads as "no
   cut", not as "meter off".[^ch13-lim-src]
2. **Run to date.** The meters are never reset during a run, so a single bad step stays in `thetamin` for the
   rest of the run.
3. **Scalars.** The passive-scalar module keeps its own hit counter, `_positivity_hits`
   ({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}), which is not printed.
4. **`conversion_trips` is not printed either.** The counter of @sec-ch04-conv4 sits among these buffers but has
   no cycle-line token, so a run must read the buffer to see it ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}).

[^ch13-lim-src]: Stated in the Limits of the source summary, `sources/gh__PR_BODIES_202-219.md`.
